text:
jamie: Quick share — ran a small perf sweep for A100-40 on AWS/GCP/Azure. Same model binary, same CUDA 12.2, same driver major, but different micro-firmware and host kernel. Seeing ~12% p95 delta between clouds, p50 much closer. attaching notes.
jamie: short table I pasted into the run notes:
```
provider  p50(ms)  p95(ms)  throughput(tokens/s)
aws       45       120      820
gcp       42       135      790
azure     44       107      855
```
(rough numbers from 512-concurrency, seq_len=1024)

sanjay: interesting — p95 spread is pretty large. did you use the same CPU pinning/affinity? NUMA config?

jamie: yes, pinned cores 0-15, isolcpus set, `taskset` in the runner. NUMA interleaving off. docker run args I used:
```
docker run --gpus all --cpuset-cpus="0-15" \ 
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ 
  redwood-infer/perf-run:canary ./run_benchmark --model resnet-like --seq 1024
```

alexa: any difference in MIG config or MIG-enabled images? That can skew tail latencies.

jamie: no MIG. Dedicated whole GPU on all clouds. Verified `nvidia-smi` shows full Tensor cores.

perf-bot: Automated summary: kernel version variance detected: aws (5.15.0-xx), gcp (5.19.0-xx), azure (5.15.0-xx). driver micro-patch: aws and gcp differ by driver build id 02 vs 03. Latency correlation with kernel scheduler ticks + firewall offload noted.

mike: cuBLAS minor version differences can cause different matmul kernel selection, especially int8/quant codepaths. Did you log `nvidia-smi -q` and `nvcc --version`?

jamie: logged both. cuBLAS reported same semantic version, but build ids different. Also saw different selected kernels in our runtime logs: `kernel: matmul_f16_optimized_v2` on azure, `matmul_f16_generic` on gcp for same opsize.

lina: could be autotuner falling back due to L2 cache associativity or TLB pressure. Did you run small warmup-only runs to populate KV cache?

jamie: yes warmup=200 tokens. Also tried increasing warmup to 1000 — p95 on gcp improved ~6% but still above aws.

sanjay: can you try disabling autotune / force kernel selection to the azure kernel on gcp as an experiment? that would prove kernel-level cause.

jamie: planned next. quick patch i used to force kernel (internal flag): `--force-kernel matmul_f16_optimized_v2` — will run a 2-hour sweep overnight and post results.

alexa: also capture perf samples (off-CPU) — `perf record -a` during the run. network stack or IRQ affinity sometimes causes weird p95 spikes across clouds.

mike: FYI we saw a driver micro-patch (build 03) that changed clock governor behavior under sustained memcopy; that reduced p95 on one benchmark last month. worth bisecting driver build id.

jamie: note to self: run driver-bisect (aws build02 <-> gcp build03), kernel-bisect (5.15 vs 5.19), and kernel-rt toggle. will post artifacts.

perf-bot: file upload: `2004712345/sweeps/` (plots + runlog.tar.gz)

lina: if you end up forcing kernel and p95 falls to azure levels, we should make a short runbook for Dedicated customers — fallback to builtin kernel map or pin to Azure-preferred kernels.

jamie: agreed. will summarize steps and open an RFC for operator flag + autosuggest in Redwood Optimize if we find a consistent pattern. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks — ping when results are in or if you want help with perf collection. :eyes:

jamie: will do. heading to run now. :rocket:
